Chapter 6: Building a Supportive Community
So, after putting in the work to transform yourself and take real steps as an entrepreneur, what comes next? Well, let’s talk about something truly powerful—community. Sure, personal effort matters, but here’s the truth: nobody really thrives on their own.
Having a supportive network is like having both a safety net and a launching pad. It’s where you find encouragement, people to keep you accountable, and access to resources you might not even know existed.
Now, when I say community, I mean it in the broadest sense. Think about mentors who can guide you, peers who are working toward similar goals, and allies who can open new doors. It might show up as a professional network, a mastermind group, or even an online forum where women help each other grow.
Try picturing your community as a garden. Each person’s growth actually feeds the whole. When one woman breaks through, she’s clearing a path for others to follow. That kind of shared momentum? It’s often what helps us push past feelings of loneliness and self-doubt, especially when we’re reaching for something big.
So, how do you actually build and nurture a supportive community?
Here are a few practical ideas:
Seek out mentors and role models—women who’ve already done what you want to do.
Join groups or organizations that connect with your career or financial interests.
Be generous: offer help and share what you know, because the more you give, the more often you’ll receive in return.
And don’t forget to celebrate other women’s successes just as loudly as you celebrate your own. That’s how you help create a culture where everyone feels there’s enough to go around.
Now, here’s something to pay attention to—not every relationship will lift you up. Sometimes, old friends or even family can reinforce doubts or hold you back from taking risks. In those moments, setting healthy boundaries or finding fresh connections isn’t just smart; it’s self-care.
And there’s something else: community isn’t just about personal growth. When women come together—maybe to push for policy changes, share resources, or simply amplify each other’s voices—they start to challenge larger, systemic barriers. That collective action can spark real change, not just for individuals, but for all of us.
So, the real takeaway? Building wealth is never just a solo journey. It’s a shared adventure, made richer by the wisdom, encouragement, and solidarity of those walking beside you.
